paras: The shooting of Hannibal Lee was the wounding of a Black man by Town Marshal Jim Walker in Pineville, Louisiana, on Saturday, December 2, 1882. Lee was reported "dangerously wounded," and the only surviving report justified the shooting by saying he had resisted arrest and assaulted the marshal.

According to the Louisiana Democrat of Alexandria, Marshal Walker shot Lee in Pineville on the Saturday before the paper's December 6 issue. The paper stated that "Lee not only resisted arrest but assaulted Walker," an account that gives only the officer's side and names no witness. The item does not say what offense Lee was being arrested for, where in town the shooting took place, or how many shots were fired.
No report of Lee's recovery or death, of an inquest, or of any action against Walker was found in the coverage.

The Louisiana Democrat printed the shooting as a two-sentence item in its local column, between a notice of a manslaughter sentence at Colfax and an advertisement for hair balsam. It identified Lee as "a colored man" and presented the marshal's justification as fact rather than as a claim. No other newspaper report of the shooting was found.
